output.headline: A sponsor with an open platform in the target's sub-sector, a deal range that fits $200M, and a record of paying upper-quartile multiples.
output.differentiator: One of three sponsors on the priority list with an open platform, alongside Nordic Capital and Welsh Carson. Its 15.5x median paid is above Nordic Capital's median.
output.why_them: Add-on to its open platform; pays upper-quartile multiples

acquirer_overview.title: A large sponsor with 18 deals since 2016 and 15 closed
points: Financial sponsor with 18 deals from 2016 to 2024. 15 of 18 closed (83%) and 17 of 18 were control deals. [T:record, K:closed_share, K:control_share]
Raised Advent Global Private Equity X, about $25 billion (2022 vintage). Approximately $100 billion AUM as of November 2025. [P:1, P:2]
Home sub-sector is Behavioral Health. 8 of 18 deals are in provider services and 10 are outside it. [B:buyer, A:angles, T:record]

strategic_fit_thesis.title: An add-on to an open platform, backed by adjacent provider deals
points: One deal in the target's own sub-sector and 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors. Sub-sector relevance is a modest factor in its likelihood. [T:record, S:sector_rel]
Its open platform in the sub-sector makes the target an add-on rather than a new bet, and size fit is a second angle. [A:angles]
Margin Improvement was a motive in 7 of 18 deals, which suits a target with a 16.8% margin. [M:margin_improvement, X:target]

precedent_activity.title: Latest sub-sector deal in 2024, plus a behavioral health record
points: Crest Care Partners: 2024, $304M Recapitalization at 9.3x EBITDA, in the target's own sub-sector. [D:MA-2024-0120]
Crown Addiction Treatment (2023, $123M Recapitalization, 14.6x) and Principal Counseling (2021, $163M Minority Investment, 13.2x), both behavioral health. [D:MA-2023-0108, D:MA-2021-0341]
Summit DSO: 2018, $303M Merger of Equals at 11.7x, its one Midwest deal. 8 of 18 deals sit in the $100M-$400M band. [D:MA-2018-0184, K:size_band]

valuation_context.title: Upper-quartile pricing is defensible; the return at the ask is thin
points: 70 comparable deals: 10.7x EV/EBITDA at the 25th percentile, 12.8x median, 15.3x at the 75th. [V:comps]
The 75th percentile is defensible: the 16.8% margin beats the comparable median of 12.9% and is above 87% of comps. [V:comps, X:target]
Advent's own median paid is 15.5x. At 5.0x leverage and a $128M equity cheque, IRR at the ask is 18.7% against a 20% target. [V:comps, V:lbo]

risk_flags.title: Return at the asking price
risk_flags.concern: IRR at the ask of 18.7% is below the 20% target. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.mitigant: A platform exit at 15.0x lifts the maximum price to $216M, against $193M at the same exit. [V:lbo]
risk_flags.reality: The bid clears the target only if it underwrites the add-on exit. [V:lbo, A:angles]

risk_flags.title: Thin Midwest footprint
risk_flags.concern: Having bought in this or a neighbouring region is a slight factor against; only 1 deal is in the target's region. [S:geo_fit, T:record]
risk_flags.mitigant: Geographic expansion was a motive in 13 of 18 deals, and 3 deals are in the Great Plains. [M:geographic_expansion, T:record]
risk_flags.reality: Geographic expansion is common across the file, so it is weak support; the region is a modest gap. [M:geographic_expansion]

risk_flags.title: Competing open platforms
risk_flags.concern: Nordic Capital and Welsh Carson also run open platforms and have more adjacent provider deals on the priority list.
risk_flags.mitigant: Advent has 7 adjacent provider deals and a 15.5x median paid. [T:record]
risk_flags.reality: Platform access is not unique to Advent, so price and certainty of closing decide; 15 of 18 deals closed. [K:closed_share]

conviction.rationale: Rests on 1 deal in the target's own sub-sector and 7 in adjacent provider sub-sectors, plus an open platform in the sub-sector that gives an add-on route. [T:record, A:angles, C:conviction]
